_README: Industry events / semiconductor conferences that can move watchlist names via product announcements, roadmap disclosures, or competitive read-through. The morning routine (CLAUDE.md) refreshes dates and 'watch' notes via web search each run and adds newly-announced events. 'tickers' = watchlist symbols with direct or read-through exposure. 'confidence': confirmed (dates verified) | approx (typical timing, verify) | rumored. Dates are ISO YYYY-MM-DD, event-local. Not investment advice.

events.name: FMS 2026 — The Future of Memory and Storage (20th anniversary)
events.watch: Added 2026-08-04 (the morning it opens — this event was MISSING from the calendar and is the most watchlist-relevant thing happening this week). Dates verified Aug 4-6, Santa Clara Convention Center; keynotes across the three days from Samsung, SK hynix, Micron and NVIDIA (Jason Hardy, VP Storage Technology, NVDA; Jin-Yub Lee, EVP Flash Product & Technology, Samsung; Jim Elliott, CRO, Sandisk). Already delivered on day 0: **SK hynix and Sandisk published the first HBF (High Bandwidth Flash) standard specification** (announced 2026-08-03) — a tier positioned between HBM and SSD, up to 512GB in 8-high/16-high NAND stacks, three performance grades spanning ~0.4TB/s to 3.0TB/s, over a UCIe chiplet interface, released through the Open Compute Project as an open industry standard rather than proprietary IP (consortium members now include Google and Tenstorrent; partnership began Aug 2025, consortium formed Feb 2026). SK hynix's own keynote (EVP Kim Chun-sung + VP Kang Uk-song, day 1) is titled 'Orchestrating Efficient AI Infrastructure through Tiered Memory in the Era of Agentic AI', and it is showing unreleased V10 375-layer 4D NAND (~2.5x power efficiency vs prior gen) with eSSD mass production guided to early next year. Why it matters to this book: HBF is a NAND-side attempt to monetise the AI memory wall, which speaks directly to @jukan05's persistent-NAND-shortage case and to the 000660/SKHY/MU/DRAM/DISK/EWY complex; watch the remaining two days for HBM4 ramp/capacity commentary from all three makers (Samsung guiding ~50% HBM capacity expansion in 2026) and for whether NVIDIA endorses a tiered-memory architecture that pulls NAND into the accelerator budget. **Updated 2026-08-04 midday (day 1, in progress) — the NVIDIA tiered-memory question above now has a scheduled answer.** NVIDIA's Jason Hardy (VP Storage Technology) delivers a JOINT keynote with ScaleFlux CEO/co-founder Hao Zhong on **Wednesday Aug 5 at 1:20pm PT**, and the published abstract is explicitly the endorsement case: flash emerging as a new memory tier for AI inference — larger models, improved GPU utilisation, lower infrastructure cost — with flash + CXL + software-defined tiering extending AI pipelines without proportional cost increase. That is NVIDIA lending its name from the demand side to the same architectural argument the SK hynix/Sandisk HBF spec makes from the supply side, and it is the single highest-value session of this week for the 000660/SKHY/MU/DRAM/DISK/EWY complex. Pricing backdrop into the remaining two days (Seoul Economic Daily, 2026-08-04): July contract prices set fresh records — PC DRAM DDR4 8Gb **$24, +14.3% MoM** (8x the June-2016 $2.90); general-purpose NAND 128Gb **$30.1, +4.3% MoM**, up 19 consecutive months; SLC NAND +35-51% on supply constraint vs MLC +4-8% as customers resist. TrendForce guides Q3 PC DRAM **+15-20% QoQ** as makers divert wafers to server/cloud, while cutting Q3 laptop shipments **-10.6% QoQ / -20.7% YoY** on elevated component cost — the price-rise and demand-destruction legs of the same cycle in one print. **Updated 2026-08-04 evening — day 1 closed, and it delivered on the supply side.** SK hynix's Kim Chun-sung / Kang Uk-song keynote ('Orchestrating Efficient AI Infrastructure through Tiered Memory in the Era of Agentic AI') was delivered as scheduled, and the company showed its **tenth-generation V10 375-layer 4D NAND publicly for the first time** at the booth (~2.5x power efficiency vs prior gen). The HBF standard spec with Sandisk (Google and Tenstorrent participating) is now formally out rather than pre-announced. Non-watchlist but the clearest read on where NAND value is migrating: **Kioxia's CM10 headlined the show floor** — the first enterprise SSD combining PCIe 6.0, 332-layer BiCS10 NAND and direct cold-plate liquid cooling, i.e. NAND being engineered into the rack's thermal budget rather than bolted on beside it. **The one thing still ahead is the one that matters most for this book: NVIDIA's Jason Hardy keynotes jointly with ScaleFlux on Wed Aug 5 at 1:20pm PT** on flash as an AI-inference memory tier. Day 1 supplied the supply-side commitment; Aug 5 is where the demand side either endorses it or doesn't, and that is the single highest-value session of the week for the 000660/SKHY/MU/DRAM/DISK/EWY complex. **Updated 2026-08-05 morning run (day 2, ~07:30 BRT / 10:30 UTC — the day opens, keynote not yet delivered).** The NVIDIA/ScaleFlux keynote is confirmed on the published agenda for **today, Wed Aug 5, 1:20pm PT (20:20 UTC)** — Jason Hardy (VP Storage Technology, NVDA) with Hao Zhong (CEO/co-founder, ScaleFlux), titled 'Memory Solutions to Scale AI Data Pipeline'. It lands roughly three hours AFTER this run's cutoff, so it is still a pending catalyst, not a result; the 17:30 BRT run is the first that can report the outcome. New colour ahead of it: ScaleFlux's pre-show disclosure frames the substance more concretely than the abstract did — it has built **drive-level storage co-designed for NVIDIA's CMX KV-cache system**, arguing KV-cache churn burns through SSD endurance and that SSD controller/firmware must be designed in concert with the KV-cache layer. That is a narrower and more falsifiable claim than 'flash is a memory tier': it says the inference stack is already forcing NAND-side silicon respins. **The genuinely new datapoint of day 2 is an absence, not an announcement: DigiTimes (2026-08-05) reports CXMT is missing from the FMS exhibitor list** while Samsung, SK hynix and Micron are all present. CXMT is the named falsifier in the EWY/000660/DISK theses (its 2026-07-27 STAR listing knocked 10.8% off the KOSPI), so its non-appearance at the industry's flagship memory show is worth logging — though read it cautiously: absence from a US trade-show floor is at least as consistent with export-control/optics caution as with any capability read, and the article body is paywalled beyond the headline claim. **Updated 2026-08-05 midday run (~12:50 BRT / 15:50 UTC, day 2 in progress).** The NVIDIA/ScaleFlux keynote ('Memory Solutions to Scale AI Data Pipeline', Jason Hardy VP Storage Technology NVDA + Hao Zhong CEO ScaleFlux) is **still ahead of this run's cutoff — 1:20pm PT = 20:20 UTC, roughly four hours out** — so for the third consecutive run it is a pending catalyst rather than a result; the 17:30 BRT run is the first that can report the outcome. **The material thing this pass surfaces is a watchlist company that was exhibiting here and had not been logged: MARVELL (added to this event's tickers).** On 08-04 at FMS, Marvell announced an AI-memory-infrastructure portfolio spanning three layers at once — **Bravera SC6** (PCIe 6.0 SSD controller, ~2x the SC5, multi-supplier NAND, sampling Q4 2026); **Structera X** (CXL memory expansion and pooling; company-reported up to 4.8x inference throughput and -82.7% time-to-first-token in GPU pooling configs, 48TB behind a single CXL switch); and **Photonic Fabric** (a shared memory tier across XPUs and racks up to 50m apart, up to 32TB of warm KV-cache offload, claimed 2-3x token throughput in the same power envelope). All figures are vendor-reported. Why it matters beyond MRVL: this is the *silicon-vendor* leg of the same tiered-memory architecture that the SK hynix/Sandisk HBF spec asserts from the supply side and that the NVIDIA keynote is expected to endorse from the demand side — three independent layers of the stack converging on flash-and-CXL-as-memory inside one trade show, which is a stronger signal than any single announcement. It also gives the optics chain a second demand vector: Photonic Fabric sells optics as memory rather than as interconnect. Macro backdrop into day 3: the KOSPI closed **+3.76% at 6,598** on ₩1.446tn of foreign buying with SK hynix up ~5.8%, and WTI fell ~6.4% on Strait-of-Hormuz reopening expectations — the memory complex is trading with the tape, not against it.

events.name: Rosenblatt 6th Annual Technology Summit: The Age of AI (Part II)
events.watch: Added 2026-08-05: broker-hosted virtual tech summit (Part I ran Jun 9-10; Part II is Aug 17-18). Watchlist relevance is narrow but dated and specific: **AAOI presents in a fireside chat on Tue Aug 18 at 11:00am ET, with Stefan Murry (CFO and Chief Strategy Officer)** — announced 2026-08-04. Calibrate expectations: this is a sell-side investor event, not a technical venue, so it produces commentary and guidance colour rather than product disclosure. Its value is timing — it falls 12 days after AAOI's Q2 print (Aug 6) and lands in the middle of the live FCC/Chinese-optical-transceiver-ban story that moved AAOI +17% on 08-04, so it is the first scheduled opportunity for management to be asked directly about import-ban exposure, 800G/1.6T capacity at the Pearland expansion, and CPO timing. A recording is posted to the company IR site afterwards.

events.name: Hot Chips 2026 (IEEE Symposium on High-Performance Chips)
events.watch: Re-checked 2026-07-31: no material change since the 07-30 pass — official program still shows speaker names attached to essentially all previously-listed talks. NVDA (5 talks): Vera CPU (Jonathon Evans & Polychronis Xekalakis); Rubin GPU 'Driving the Era of Agentic AI' (Manas Mandal, Rajballav Dash & Ravi Manyam); BlueField-4 (Idan Burstein); Spectrum-X multiplane networking (Gilad Shainer); the heterogeneous GPU-LPU design is titled 'Think Fast' LPU accelerator (Igor Arsovski & Santosh Raghavan). AVGO (1 talk): Thor Ultra Ethernet NIC (Hemal Shah). AMD (4 talks, non-watchlist but competitive read-through): MI400 architecture (Alan Smith & Maiyuran Subramaniam), MI400 system architecture (Steve Scott, David Riddoch & Krishna Doddapaneni), secure SoC (Jaideep Dastidar & Thomas To), Versal RF (Jeff Cuppett). Keynote confirmed: Daniel Rosenband (Waymo), 'Compute in Motion: Challenges of Autonomous Driving.' Second keynote still unnamed. Two tutorials now have topics (memory technology & AI data requirements; RISC-V standards and adoption) but speakers still TBD. MRVL, TSM, GFS: still NO confirmed talks in the official program — read-through for those three remains indirect (foundry/interconnect layer under NVDA/AVGO/AMD silicon), unchanged from prior note. Also present, non-watchlist context: Google 8th-gen TPU, Meta MTIA. Re-verified 2026-08-03: dates confirmed Aug 23-25 at Memorial Auditorium, Stanford (plus online); program still lists two tutorials, two keynotes and ~25 architect presentations from AMD, Intel, NVIDIA, Google and others. The SECOND KEYNOTE REMAINS UNNAMED — the one open slot in the program and the only place a genuine surprise can still enter. No change to any watchlist-relevant talk since the 07-31 pass. Re-checked again 2026-08-03 evening: second keynote still unnamed, no program changes. New: @firstadopter (tae kim, Tier 1) confirmed on 08-01 that he is attending, so expect first-hand written coverage of the NVDA Vera/Rubin/BlueField-4/Spectrum-X talks rather than only the official program. Re-verified 2026-08-04 morning against the official program page: dates and every watchlist-relevant talk unchanged (NVDA x4 — Vera CPU, Rubin GPU, BlueField-4, Spectrum-X multiplane; AVGO x1 — Thor Ultra Ethernet NIC; still no MRVL/TSM/GFS talks), Rosenband/Waymo keynote confirmed, and the SECOND KEYNOTE IS STILL UNNAMED — five consecutive passes with that slot open, which by now is itself the signal: either a late-breaking announcement or a low-key fill. 19 days out. Re-checked 2026-08-04 midday: official program unchanged again — dates Aug 23-25 at Memorial Auditorium (plus online), two keynotes / two tutorials / ~25 architect talks, every watchlist-relevant talk identical (NVDA x4, AVGO x1 Thor Ultra Ethernet NIC, still no MRVL/TSM/GFS), and the SECOND KEYNOTE IS STILL UNNAMED — a sixth consecutive pass with that slot open, 19 days out. Treat it as a low-information slot now rather than a pending catalyst; it will be re-checked but will not be re-narrated each run unless it fills. Re-checked 2026-08-05 morning: seventh consecutive pass, second keynote still unnamed, dates and all watchlist-relevant talks unchanged — logged as a stamp only, per the standing note not to re-narrate this slot until it fills. 18 days out. Re-verified 2026-08-05 midday against the official program: dates unchanged (Aug 23-25, Memorial Auditorium, Stanford), Rosenband/Waymo keynote confirmed for Mon Aug 24 2:15pm, and the **second keynote is still unnamed — eighth consecutive pass**. Logged as a stamp only, per the standing note. No watchlist-relevant talk changed. 18 days out.

events.name: SPIE Optics + Photonics 2026
events.watch: Added 2026-08-03: dates verified against SPIE's own listing — conferences Aug 23-27, exhibition Aug 25-27, courses Aug 23-26. Calibrate expectations: this is SPIE's RESEARCH-tier optics meeting (optical engineering, nanophotonics, optoelectronic materials, quantum), NOT the datacom/telecom product venue — ECOC (Sep 20-24) and OFC (Mar 2027) remain the real catalyst windows for CPO, 1.6T transceivers and InP-laser roadmaps. Value here is early technical signal on InP/photonic-substrate materials and packaging that shows up as product 12-24 months later, which matters given the InP substrate shortage now documented in the SIVE file (AXT/Lumentum LTA to 2031, Lumentum CEO citing a >30% demand-supply gap). Runs exactly concurrent with Hot Chips 2026 (Aug 23-25) — the same week carries both the compute-silicon and the photonics-research read.

events.name: SEMICON Taiwan 2026
events.watch: Added 2026-07-30: major Asia-Pacific fab-equipment/WFE show, ~5 days after AI Infra Summit and ~2.5 weeks before ECOC — same September AI-infra/semi catalyst cluster. 2026 program spans 13 themes incl. AI chips, advanced packaging, 3DIC, chiplets, heterogeneous integration; watch for TSMC capacity/pricing commentary and equipment-order read-through. Re-verified 2026-08-04 against SEMI's own release: dates confirmed **Sep 2-4 at Nangang Halls 1 & 2**, with the **conference program running wider than the exhibition — Aug 31 through Sep 4**, so the first TSMC/supply-chain commentary can land two days before the show floor opens. Record scale this year: **1,300+ exhibitors and 4,300+ booths (both all-time highs), 100,000+ attendees from 65 countries.** Named themes now include **silicon photonics** alongside AI chips, advanced packaging and quantum — which makes this a secondary read for the SIVE/SOI optics chain, not only a TSM/GFS event, though ECOC (Sep 20-24) remains the real optics catalyst. 29 days out.

events.name: AI Infra Summit 2026
events.watch: Speaker list expanded to 400+ as of 2026-07-27 scan (8,000+ attendees, 300+ sessions, 8 stages) across 5 tracks: Compute, Data Movement, Physical AI, Data & Models, AI Data Center. Named speakers now include Lip-Bu Tan (CEO, Intel) and Dave Lazovsky (EVP, Marvell) on the main stage, plus Jeff Dean (Google), Kripa Krishnan (VP, Meta AI Infrastructure) — direct read-through for INTC and MRVL specifically, not just the thematic complex, alongside NVDA/AVGO/WULF/META exposure already logged. Falls 5 days before ECOC 2026, inside the same September AI-infra catalyst window.

events.name: ECOC 2026 (European Conference on Optical Communication)
events.watch: THE optics event for the small-caps: CPO (co-packaged optics), 800G/1.6T transceivers, EML/DFB laser and InP-substrate progress. Direct catalyst window for Sivers (CPO lasers) and Soitec (photonics substrates); DSP/optics read-through for MRVL & AVGO. Lumentum/Coherent disclosures here reset the whole InP supply picture.

events.name: OCP Global Summit 2026 (Open Compute Project)
events.watch: Hyperscaler datacenter standards — rack power/cooling, networking fabrics, custom silicon, optics adoption. Meta is a core OCP driver (capex read-through); networking/optics read-through for AVGO & MRVL; datacenter-infrastructure read-through for WULF's HPC-conversion thesis.

events.name: SEMICON West 2026
events.watch: Dates confirmed 2026-07-22 via the official SEMI organizer site (Pre-Show Day Mon Oct 12, show floor Oct 13-15). Fab-equipment/WFE industry event, almost exactly overlapping the existing OCP Global Summit (Oct 12-15, San Jose) — same catalyst week. Relevant to TSM (leading-edge capacity/pricing commentary) and GFS (specialty-foundry, onshoring/CHIPS Act positioning).

events.name: IEDM 2026 (72nd IEEE International Electron Devices Meeting)
events.watch: Added 2026-07-30: premier device-physics/process-tech conference, theme 'Devices at the Heart of the Intelligence Revolution.' Expect next-node transistor (GAA/CFET) and advanced-packaging/substrate papers directly relevant to Soitec's SOI/substrate roadmap plus TSM/INTC/GFS process roadmaps. Detailed accepted-paper program not yet released; dates flagged 'subject to change' by some listings — verify closer to the event.

events.name: CES 2027
events.watch: Consumer + edge-AI keynotes; NVIDIA typically opens with a roadmap/keynote. Broad AI-infrastructure tone-setter for the year. 60th-anniversary edition.

events.name: OFC 2027 (Optical Fiber Communication Conference & Exposition)
events.watch: Added 2026-07-30: the largest global optics show — the semiannual bookend to ECOC for CPO/transceiver/InP-laser roadmap disclosures (1.6T/3.2T transceivers, co-packaged optics), directly feeding the Sivers/Soitec thesis.

events.name: NVIDIA GTC 2027
events.watch: NVIDIA's flagship — next-gen architecture (post-Rubin) roadmap, networking (NVLink/Spectrum), and increasingly CPO/optics partners. The single biggest AI-infra catalyst of the year; read-through across the entire watchlist, especially the optics chain if NVDA advances co-packaged optics.
